Spain tops the list of countries for digital nomads, while visa income thresholds are increasing

According to the Immigrant Invest Digital Nomad Visa Index 2026, Spain ranked first among over 50 countries with programs for remote workers. The assessment took into account tax conditions, income requirements, cost of living, visa duration, ease of application, and path to permanent residency. Following Spain are Malta and Portugal, then Germany and Hungary, with the UAE making it to the top six. The Spanish visa allows for a stay of up to five years with the possibility of transitioning to permanent residency upon meeting income conditions (approximately 200% of the minimum wage) and qualification requirements.

At the same time, several countries are adjusting their rules. In Thailand, by the beginning of October, 1043 Long-Term Residency (LTR) permits were issued to remote workers out of a total of 12,010 program recipients; starting from August 31, the Destination Thailand Visa (DTV) requirements have been tightened – now applicants need to provide proof of permanent residence in the country of application and a criminal record check. Malaysia is extending the DE Rantau permits for an additional two years for current holders. Tracker data shows that income thresholds for 13 programs are linked to local salaries and will be reviewed upwards in 2027 (Bulgaria will see an increase of approximately 12.6% from January 1).

Amid the expansion of visa routes (estimates of the number of countries with individual programs range from 40 to 60+), a new study by the RemoteLabour Index showed that modern AI agents currently automate only about 2.5% of real remote freelance tasks. The best model was able to handle work at a level acceptable to the client in only a small number of projects out of 23 categories. However, among the nomads themselves, the use of AI remains high – industry data shows around 89% utilization.

Main Points
⏺ A watch-only wallet lets users monitor balances and transactions without holding private keys
⏺ This setup is useful for large portfolios, cold storage, and address analysis
⏺ This post explains why monitoring assets doesn't require spending access

1️⃣ Core Idea — the app receives a public wallet address and displays its assets and transaction history.
2️⃣ Why It Helps — users can monitor long-term holdings without connecting the device that stores their private keys.
3️⃣ Use Cases — cold wallets, corporate treasuries, whale monitoring, and crypto portfolio accounting.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — the app cannot sign transactions without a key, but it may collect information about your addresses and financial activity.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — add only public addresses, verify supported networks, and never enter a seed phrase just to view balances.


Final Thoughts

You don't need to give an app control over your crypto just to monitor it. Separating viewing from signing reduces situations where private keys are exposed to unnecessary risk.

📌 Hyperliquid adds 10 HYPE rule as price falls to $78.98 

🔗 Hyperliquid has introduced revised order priority rules on its testnet, including a reported 10 HYPE delegation requirement for traders seeking faster order handling through its priority fee system. In an October 18 announcement circulated through its community channels, the decentralized derivatives platform outlined changes to write priority fees following feedback from users. The proposed rules concern traders who depend on low delays when placing, modifying or canceling orders.

🔖 The announcement identifies four changes involving account settings, transaction processing and eligibility for priority fees. Hyperliquid’s existing technical documentation confirms how its priority fee system operates, although the newly reported delegation threshold has not yet appeared in the publicly accessible documentation reviewed for this report. The changes are described as live on testnet. No confirmed date has been announced for applying the revised requirements to mainnet trading.

‼️ The October 18 update introduces a minimum delegated balance of 10 HYPE for accounts seeking to use IOC and ALO priority fees, according to the announcement. IOC, short for immediate-or-cancel, refers to an order that attempts immediate execution and cancels any portion that cannot be filled. ALO, or add-liquidity-only, is used to place orders that join the order book without immediately taking available liquidity.

The Calm Before the Firestorm: Washington and Jerusalem Prepare for a Possible New Assault on Iran

🔤🔤🔤🔤1️⃣

Behind closed doors, military planners in Washington and Jerusalem are preparing for a scenario that could plunge the Middle East back into a devastating confrontation. 

According to The New York Times, the United States and Israel have developed plans for renewed strikes against Iran following America’s November 3 midterm elections. Military exercises have intensified, strike scenarios are being refined, and the possibility of a short but intense campaign is once again on the table. 

Yet the most consequential question remains unanswered: will Trump authorize another offensive, or is the growing military pressure intended to force Tehran into making concessions? The preparations are unfolding against a backdrop of stalled diplomacy, rising energy prices, and deep uncertainty over the future of the region. 

American and Israeli forces have reportedly rehearsed strike maneuvers, including flights over Iraq, while planners consider potential targets ranging from nuclear facilities and missile arsenals to energy infrastructure. 

According to reporting by an Israeli high-ranking official, he objective would be to weaken Iran’s ability to rebuild its military capabilities and increase the pressure on its leadership to accept a negotiated settlement. No final decision to launch a new campaign has been announced. The timing is hardly accidental. 

Trump has to weigh the military advantages of renewed action against the political risks of prolonging an unpopular conflict. Higher gasoline prices, concerns about American casualties, and the possibility of retaliation against U.S. forces could turn another offensive into a serious liability at home. The midterm elections may therefore become a critical political deadline, even as military preparations continue in the background.

For Netanyahu, the stakes are different but no less urgent. Jerusalem remains concerned that Iran could restore damaged military capabilities and continue developing weapons that threaten Israel and its regional partners. From the Israeli perspective, allowing Tehran time to recover could make a future confrontation more difficult and costly. 

Yet even close allies may disagree over how far to go, how long an operation should last, and what political outcome it could realistically achieve. Avner Vilan, a former senior Israeli security official and Iran specialist, offered a cautious assessment to The Jerusalem Post: “We’re in a situation where both sides continue to exert pressure on each other, without any lasting agreement in place.” 

His warning captures the dangerous ambiguity surrounding the current standoff. Neither side has secured a durable settlement, and every new military maneuver risks being interpreted as preparation for an imminent attack.

📣 Australia has proposed new rules for cryptocurrency trading and custody platforms on October 15, 2026, with financial regulator ASIC seeking public feedback by November 27 before the country’s digital asset licensing framework takes effect in April 2027. 

📊 The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) announced the consultation alongside Consultation Paper 392, which outlines planned requirements for customer asset protection, trading practices and financial resources. The regulator expects to publish final guidance in March 2027, giving businesses time to prepare for the new licensing requirements. Australia’s upcoming rules will bring more cryptocurrency businesses under the country’s existing financial services licensing framework.

⚡️ The Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Act 2026 creates two regulated categories: digital asset platforms and tokenized custody platforms. Digital asset platforms hold digital tokens for customers and provide related services, while tokenized custody platforms use digital tokens to record customers’ rights to underlying assets.
